ideas: Build a one-offer landing page for your own job search (one primary action: book a call) by running the skill's Part A intake and seven-part output format before any code, then let the agent build it section by section.
Fork the repo and rewrite the 'make it yours' design-values section with your own fonts, colors, spacing and motion, so every agent-built client page starts from your house style.
Run its B10 ship requirements and quick checklist against two past client sites (hotel, e-commerce) and fix what's missing: 404 page, og:image, skip link, form validation, alt text.

Turn the B11 tagline reveal (word-by-word IntersectionObserver, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), prefers-reduced-motion fallback) into a reusable React component for a new portfolio project, keeping ai-daily-radar's design as is.
Paste the SKILL.md into a Codex AGENTS.md and give the same landing-page brief to it, impeccable and hallmark, then compare the three results to learn which rules actually change the output.

ideas: Install the macOS desktop app on the Mac mini, open one Android or Swift project, and run two pi sessions in separate git-worktree workspaces on the same task, then merge the better branch.
Have the agent build a SPEC.md graph for a client app with its spec tools, so the intent behind screens and APIs survives between sessions and new agents can pick it up.
Point it at the Agent Skills you already keep (CLI-Anything and the archived skill repos) and check which ones pi reads in place without changes.
Use its PR flow on a repo with GitHub Actions: open a PR described from the plan, watch CI in the topbar, and hand a failing check back to the agent to fix.

Connect one or two MCP servers through pi's mcp.json with per-call approval, and try the before/after UI mockup comments as a lighter way to review agent-made UI changes; it's an early incubator release, so keep it off production repos at first.
